controls.answer: The information security policy 4.0 was approved by management on 14 July 2026. It states why security matters to the business, sets its objectives, and derives the security requirements each year from the business plan, customer contracts and German law. It is published on the intranet with nine supporting standards and procedures, and change notices go to employees and, through the supplier portal, to suppliers. No document says what happens when someone breaks the policy, and the encryption standard it names has not been reviewed since March 2022.

controls.answer: The encryption standard allows only methods the national cyber security authority recommends: AES with at least 128-bit keys for stored data, RSA with at least 3072 bits or elliptic curves with at least 256 bits, and SHA-256 or stronger. Laptops use full-disk encryption and connections use TLS 1.2 or newer. It covers how keys are created, stored, withdrawn and renewed. It was approved in March 2022 with a yearly review and has not been reviewed since.

requirements.reason: The approved methods follow the national authority's recommendations, but the standard was approved in March 2022 with a yearly review, so it is out of date.

citations.quote: We use only encryption methods that the national cyber security authority recommends: AES with keys of at least 128 bits for stored data, RSA with at least 3072 bits or elliptic curves with at least 256 bits for key exchange and signatures, and SHA-256 or stronger for hashing.
